name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Switching a server off now actually stops its titles playing, and the config page reports whether federation is working. Disabling a server previously only stopped syncing: the dynamic provider refused to serve a source, but Jellyfin independently exposed whatever URL was stamped on the item as a static source, so titles kept streaming from a server the admin had just switched off. Reconciliation now clears that URL - and restores it when the server comes back. Crucially it resolves against every source in priority order rather than just the primary: sources are ordered by priority and never re-ordered by enabled state, so on a deduped title (the same film matched across servers) the preferred server can be off while another still serves it, and keying off the primary alone would have stripped the Play button from an item that was perfectly playable elsewhere - breaking the exact redundancy dedup exists to provide. Toggling the switch now also reconciles immediately instead of leaving the change to take effect up to an hour later on the next scheduled sync. Separately, the page now shows the outcome of the last sync: green when every source refreshed, red with the reason when one did not, plus a note that content from an unreachable server was preserved rather than deleted. Until now that information existed only in the server log, so a library that had quietly stopped updating looked exactly like a healthy one - which is how a switched-off server went unnoticed here for hours. A per-server refresh that throws now records that failure too, instead of leaving the banner showing the previous success. Five tests cover the enabled/disabled source selection, including the deduped-fallback case.
